turns.en: Right. But I think the product leader is a really interesting addition there. You can't just have this team off to the side without a product leader overseeing that work.
turns.zh: 没错。但我认为产品负责人这个角色非常重要，不能让团队独立运作而没有产品负责人来监督工作。

turns.speaker: Marty Cagan
turns.en: That's so true because one of the things I really learned with INSPIRED was that it wasn't enough to have the teams do their job. They needed leadership to do their job. So it is both. And that's why I was saying we don't frame it as top-down, bottom-up for that. We frame it as each group doing their job. And when that happens, it's actually a beautiful thing.
turns.zh: 确实如此。我在INSPIRED项目中深切体会到，仅靠团队自主完成工作是不够的，还需要领导力的支持。因此这两者缺一不可。这也是为什么我们不把它定义为自上而下或自下而上，而是强调每个团队各司其职。当这种协同发生时，效果才会显著。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: We're going to link to a post that you wrote, Product Leadership Theater, which talks about how people do this actually badly and what it looks like when it's just pretend versus actually doing it right.
turns.zh: 我们会链接到你撰写的《产品领导力剧场》一文，文中探讨了人们在实践中如何误解产品领导力，以及真正做好产品领导力的标准。

turns.speaker: Marty Cagan
turns.en: Good.
turns.zh: 好的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay. And then what are some of these principles, just to touch on a couple and a few-
turns.zh: 好的。那么这些原则具体包括哪些方面？先简单提几点——

turns.speaker: Marty Cagan
turns.en: Just stop me, but there's a set of principles around the more cultural things, like innovation is more important than predictability. That's a principle. That learning is more important than failure. The principles are more important than process. Some examples of that. In terms of teams, empowered with problems to solve. That's one of your foundational principles. We talked about that, this idea of real ownership, real sense of ownership so that it's theirs. Well, of course in discovery you'd recognize all the principles, but it's about addressing product risks. It's about embracing quick experimentation. It's about testing ideas responsibly. These are principles. And then I did mention a couple of the delivery principles, things like small frequent uncoupled releases. For most companies that's CI/CD, instrumentation of everything, monitoring of everything. These are delivery principles. So none of these should surprise you 'cause they are what's consistent in the good companies that we know, but these are the things that we think matter.
turns.zh: 就打断我一下吧，但关于更多文化层面的原则，比如创新比可预测性更重要——这就是一项原则。学习比失败更重要。原则比流程更重要。举几个例子来说。就团队而言，赋予他们自主解决问题的权力。这是你们的基本原则之一。我们曾探讨过“真正的所有权”这个概念，即让产品真正属于团队成员。当然，在探索阶段，你会意识到所有这些原则的重要性，但重点在于应对产品风险，拥抱快速实验，负责任地测试创意。这些都是原则。然后我提到了几个交付原则，比如小而频繁的解耦式发布。对于大多数公司来说，这就是持续集成/持续交付（CI/CD），全流程监控等。这些都是交付原则。这些原则应该不难理解，因为它们正是我们所熟知的优秀公司的共通之处，但正是这些原则至关重要。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: That's awesome. And I imagine people listening to this, if they're in that 10% or 20% of companies that you describe as doing this well are just like, of course. And then the rest are just like, no, there's no way we're going to be able to do that.
turns.zh: 太棒了。我想听众中如果有10%或20%的公司能把这些做得很好，他们肯定会深有共鸣。而其他公司可能就会觉得，这根本不可能做到。

turns.speaker: Marty Cagan
turns.en: You have to realize in most of the rest of the world, they release monthly or mostly quarterly. Think about that. Quarterly releases. Think about it. You cannot take care of your customers. You cannot learn at the pace you need to. By the way, quality is going to be terrible in that model.
turns.zh: 你要意识到，在世界上大多数其他地方，他们每月发布一次，或者主要按季度发布。想想看。季度发布周期。想想看。在这种模式下，你无法满足客户需求，也无法以所需的速度学习。顺便说一句，质量也会很糟糕。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I don't want to go on this tangent necessarily, but I know in some cases, like a quarterly release, like Shopify as an example, they have seasonal releases like the winter launch and the summer launch.
turns.zh: 我不想在这方面深入探讨，但我知道在某些情况下，比如Shopify，他们有季节性发布，比如冬季发布和夏季发布。

turns.speaker: Marty Cagan
turns.en: And salesforce.com has a big... But don't confuse the actual releasing by the teams with the marketing releases. So it's very normal and I think wise to batch. Because look, most product teams are releasing on the order of 20 times per day. You're going to do a marketing release 20 times a day? That would be useless. So it makes sense to have messaging on a periodic basis, but good companies, by the time they message it, it's live. It's been coming out. We may have released some things dark as you know, but we've got it in production solid. We've proven each thing probably with an AB test.
turns.zh: 而Salesforce.com则有大型发布……但别把团队的实际发布和营销发布混为一谈。所以批量发布是完全正常且明智的做法。因为看看大多数产品团队每天发布20次左右。你怎么能一天发布20次营销内容呢？那根本没用。所以定期发布信息是有意义的，但优秀的公司到发布信息时，产品已经上线了。产品可能已经在灰度测试中了，但我们已经在生产环境中验证过每个功能了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Airbnb is actually in that same model. Most of the stuff they announced every couple times a year is already out or an experiment to most people. One thing I wanted to clarify, so you call this the product operating model. There's also this role product ops, which you touched on a little bit. Any thoughts on product ops? We've had a few guests here talk about it.
turns.zh: Airbnb实际上也采用了同样的模式。他们每年发布的多数新功能，要么已经上线，要么对大多数人来说只是实验。我想澄清一下，所以你把这称为产品运营模式。还有产品运营这个角色，你也稍微提到了几句。对产品运营有什么看法吗？我们这里有几位嘉宾谈过这个话题。

turns.speaker: Marty Cagan
turns.en: It's tricky. First of all, some people have asked me, is product ops the same as product operating model? No. That was just a very unfortunate name conflict, but product ops is more analogous to DevOps and design ops, that's all. Now, can you use product ops in the product operating model? Absolutely, if you're using one of the definitions that are part of the model. So for example, the heart of product ops in the good companies I know is user research and data analysts. And the only difference is they're now brought together under one product ops leader. That's all. That that is the same. How long has that been with us, Lenny? More than 20 years. Companies have had user research teams and have had data analyst teams to help you make decisions qualitatively and help you make teams quantitatively. So that's not new at all, but it is good. And I think there is some amount of value about bringing that in. (01:12:52): Some companies, of course, they interpret and define product ops very differently. A lot of them unfortunately think of it, they focus on the whole phrase of process in governance. That's a huge red flag and I try to tell people, if that's what you see, run. Don't walk away from that. The other thing that's going on in a lot of companies, it is amazing to me how creative companies can be to try to find a way to justify giving product managers assistance because the product manager says too much work, which is really ironic to me 'cause they're usually feature teams that are saying this and I'm like, "It's not even enough for your job." But anyway, they're like, "Too much work." And so they're like, "Well, we need help." And so for a while, they would all have these little associate product managers. And then a lot of companies they have, oh, we also have product owners. (01:13:51): Product manager and product owner makes no sense. Huge anti-pattern. Today a lot of companies use the same excuse, but its product manager has product ops people to do the dirty work. No. And honestly, I would not want to be one of those people because I think they're very vulnerable right now.
turns.zh:
这确实挺复杂的。首先，有人问我，产品运营（Product Ops）和产品运营模式（Product Operating Model）是一回事吗？不是的。这不过是一个非常不幸的命名冲突，但产品运营更类似于DevOps和设计运营，仅此而已。那么，你能在产品运营模式中应用产品运营吗？当然可以，只要你采用的是该模式中的某个定义。比如，在我所知的优秀公司里，产品运营的核心是用户研究和数据分析师。唯一的不同在于，现在这些角色被统一归入一位产品运营负责人的管理之下。这两者本质上是一样的。Lenny，这项理念在我们这里已经存在多久了？超过20年了。很多公司一直有用户研究团队和数据分析团队，帮助团队做出定性决策和定量分析。这并非新鲜事物，但确实有其价值。关键在于如何将这些资源整合起来。

（01:12:52）：当然，有些公司对产品运营的理解大相径庭。很多公司不幸将其狭隘地定义为流程与治理。这是个危险信号，我总是告诫人们，如果你看到这种情况，赶紧离开。这类公司还存在另一种现象：面对产品经理抱怨工作量过大的情况，创意型公司总能想方设法为产品经理配备助手。这真是讽刺啊，因为通常是功能团队在抱怨，而我会说：“这点工作量对你的职责来说根本不够。” 但他们还是说：“工作量太大了。”于是就有了“助理产品经理”之类的角色。还有很多公司引入了“产品负责人”（Product Owner），但产品经理和产品负责人之间的界限根本说不通。这完全是反模式。

（01:13:51）：产品经理和产品负责人混为一谈简直是胡说八道。如今很多公司用同样的借口，比如“让产品运营人员做脏活累活”。不行，说真的，我可不想成为那类人中的一个，因为我觉得他们现在处境非常脆弱。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I've changed my mind on product ops. One reason is because I also was like, "I don't need another person in the loop on everything I'm doing. I just want to have..." I don't know why I would do that even though I have endless work and I have working crazy hours. But I think one of the great things about product ops people that I talk to is there's not many of them. You need one often to do a ton and to help a lot of different teams, so it's not like a team that just grows like crazy.
turns.zh: 我对产品运营的看法有所改变。一个原因是，我也曾想：“我不需要再多一个人，监督我做的每一件事。我只想……” 我不知道自己为什么会这么想，尽管我工作繁忙，工作时间极不规律。但我认为与我交流过的产品运营人员有一个优点：他们数量很少。通常需要一个人，才能承担大量工作，帮助多个团队，这不像团队会疯狂扩张。

turns.speaker: Marty Cagan
turns.en: That's what I like. Same with user research, by the way, and you had a very good guest on that I think tried to make that point as well, a small high leverage group. So it works for data analysts and it works for user research where they are helping the teams do the work they need to do, but that's where it really depends what they're doing. I will tell you I've seen too many companies where the product leaders are not doing their job, so what they do is they hire product ops to try to do their job. They're the ones now responsible for educating the product managers. That's just not good.
turns.zh: 这正是我喜欢的。顺便说一句，用户研究也是如此。我记得我们请过一位嘉宾，他也试图强调这一点——一个小型高效能团队。产品运营和用户研究的效果都很好，因为他们帮助团队完成必要工作，但关键在于具体职责如何分配。我可以告诉你，我见过太多产品负责人不尽职的情况，结果就雇佣产品运营来替他们工作。这简直是本末倒置。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I have just a few more questions before we get to our very exciting lightning round. Actually, maybe just one more question. We'll see where this goes. So I've mentioned this earlier that a lot of startup founders are just like, "I do not need product managers. I'm not going to hire them ever. Or maybe I'll wait until I have hundreds of engineers." But then I find many of them change their mind, bring in a PM and they're like, "Oh wow, this is amazing. Why didn't I do this earlier? This person, it's exactly what I needed." And these are guests I've had on the podcast that were like, "We don't need PMs." And then they get one and they're like, "Okay, I see. This is great." Do you have any advice for founders that are in this boat of just like, I don't want product managers, they're going to screw us up, they're going to slow us down? Any advice for this?
turns.zh: 在我们进入激动人心的闪电问答环节之前，我还有几个问题想问。实际上，也许就一个问题。看看情况如何吧。我之前提到过，很多创业者会说：“我不需要产品经理。我永远不会雇佣他们。或者等我们有几百名工程师了再考虑。” 但后来我发现，很多创业者后来改变了主意，引入了产品经理，然后感叹：“哇，太棒了。我为什么不早点这么做？这个人正是我们需要的。” 我播客中邀请过的嘉宾起初也说“我们不需要产品经理”，结果引入后又惊呼：“太好了，我早该这么做了。” 对于那些认为“不需要产品经理，他们会拖慢我们进度”的创业者，你有什么建议吗？

turns.speaker: Marty Cagan
turns.en: Yeah. Well, first of all, I'm one of the people that tries to discourage them from hiring product managers too soon because a lot of them make the mistake of hiring them too soon. Now, realize what we're talking about here, again, the whole discussion we've had, this is other layer to, I'm talking about a real product manager. If they're using them as project manager, which a lot of times they are, well, I would tell them they're overpaying, but okay, you can get some help for project management. That's not a good use of the CEO's time. But if they're a real product manager and they're worried about value and viability, that is the founder's job. So the founder should be doing that and needs to be doing that, and it usually causes conflict if they bring in a real product manager too soon. It's too many cooks in the kitchen. (01:16:45): You need to reach a certain scale before it helps you to have other people responsible for value and viability. That all assumes that they understand real product management, otherwise it's going to lead to very different symptoms.
turns.zh: 嗯，首先，我会劝阻他们过早雇佣产品经理，因为很多公司都犯了过早引入的错误。再说一次，我们整个讨论的核心是真正的产品经理。如果他们把产品经理当作项目经理用（很多公司都这样），那我会说他们花钱太多了，但可以找人帮忙管理项目。这不是 CEO 的时间该花在的地方。但如果是真正的产品经理，而他们又担心产品价值和可行性，那就是创始人的职责了。所以创始人应该亲自做这件事，如果过早引入产品经理，通常会引发冲突。就像厨房里太多厨师了。（01:16:45）：你需要达到一定规模后，再引入其他负责价值和可行性的人才有用。这前提是他们理解真正的产品管理，否则会出现完全不同的状况。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: So I think one piece of advice here is after product-market fit is a better time to hire a product manager. Otherwise, they're just between you and the product and it slows everything down, right?
turns.zh: 所以我认为，在产品市场匹配之后再雇佣产品经理更合适。否则，他们就会成为你和产品之间的阻碍，拖慢一切进展，对吧？

turns.speaker: Marty Cagan
turns.en: Yeah. Remember, usually as soon as you get product-market fit, you're working on it for other products and other markets, and so it's an ongoing thing, but while it's small, it usually is most useful just to look at the number of engineers. At a certain number of engineers, usually 20 to 25, it's a lot better if the co-founder is the product person for that.
turns.zh: 是的。记住，通常一旦实现了产品市场匹配，你就会为其他产品和市场而努力，这是一个持续的过程。但在公司规模小的时候，通常让联合创始人担任产品角色最有效。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Awesome. I was going to ask you if you have a heuristic for engineers and so thank you for preempting that. That's essentially all I had to chat about, Marty. Do you have anything else that you think would be interesting to share or touch on or leave listeners with before we get to a very exciting lightning round?
turns.zh: 太棒了。我本来想问你对工程师有没有启发性建议，所以谢谢你抢先回答。基本上我就想聊这些，马蒂。你还有什么想和听众分享或留给他们的内容吗？在我们进入激动人心的闪电问答环节之前。

turns.speaker: Marty Cagan
turns.en: Honestly, Lenny, we talked about so many big topics. I'm worried that may have overwhelmed people, I hope not. Because you asked all the hardest topics.
turns.zh: 说实话，伦尼，我们讨论了太多大话题。我担心可能会让听众应接不暇，希望不会。因为你问的都是最难的问题。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Well, good job me. Good job you. With that, we've reached our very exciting lightning round. Are you ready?
turns.zh: 嗯，我干得不错。你也干得不错。到此为止，我们进入激动人心的闪电问答环节了。准备好了吗？

turns.speaker: Marty Cagan
turns.en: Sure.
turns.zh: 好的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: What are two or three books that you've recommended most to other people?
turns.zh: 你向别人推荐过最多的两三本书是什么？

turns.speaker: Marty Cagan
turns.en: I love the new book from Tony Fadell called Build. It's a wonderful book and he's describing the product model, but for hardware devices and his perspective was fabulous. He had a front row seat to some of the most iconic products in the world, the iPod, the iPhone, the Nest devices. Love it. So I loved his book and I've been recommending it to all kinds of people. Another one I really liked is, do you know Tim Urban, the guy behind Wait But Why?
turns.zh: 我超爱托尼·法德尔（Tony Fadell）的新书《Build》。这是一本很棒的书，他描述的是硬件产品的开发模式，而他对此的见解堪称卓越。他曾参与开发了世界上最具标志性的产品，比如iPod、iPhone、Nest设备等。太爱这本书了！所以我一直向各种人推荐它。另外，我还特别喜欢蒂姆·厄本（Tim Urban），你知道他吗？他是《Wait But Why》博客的创始人。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Absolutely.
turns.zh: 绝对的。

turns.speaker: Marty Cagan
turns.en: I just love the way this guy thinks. And he wrote a book called What's Our Problem? that I found really provocative. Challenged me in a hundred different ways, so love that.
turns.zh: 我特别喜欢这个人的思考方式。他写了一本书叫《What's Our Problem?》，里面提出的观点很发人深省，挑战了我的认知，真是太棒了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I've been reading about his book writing process as he was writing it over the many years and it was just quite a journey he went on to make that book happen. Do you have a favorite recent movie or TV show that you really enjoyed?
turns.zh: 我一直在阅读他写书的全过程，发现这本书的诞生实在不易。你们最近有没有特别喜欢的电影或电视剧？

turns.speaker: Marty Cagan
turns.en: Lenny, you couldn't ask that to a worst person 'cause I watch almost nothing, so not a good one for that.
turns.zh: 伦尼，你问这个问题可太难为我了，因为我几乎不看电视，所以没法推荐。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Great. I think that's often for the best. Do you have a favorite interview question that you either use yourself or find useful when interviewing folks, product managers especially?
turns.zh: 太好了。我觉得这反而是件好事。你们有没有特别喜欢的面试问题，要么自己常用，要么觉得在面试产品经理时很有用？

turns.speaker: Marty Cagan
turns.en: Well, given how much interviewing I do, I stopped giving out my real favorite questions because they became online. But I do have a go-to question that I pretty much start with everybody and I want to know if they can even define the job of a product manager.
turns.zh: 嗯，鉴于我面试次数太多了，我已经不再分享自己最喜欢的面试问题了，因为它们都被曝光了。但我确实有一个常用的开场问题，我几乎对每个人都会问这个问题：你能否定义产品经理的工作职责吗？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: What do you find in the answer and what do you look for? Is it just how close they are to your version of a product manager?
turns.zh: 从他们的回答中能发现什么？你如何判断他们的理解是否接近你的定义？

turns.speaker: Marty Cagan
turns.en: I can tell where they learned from their answer, that's all. They don't have to give my answer. They just shouldn't give the old feature team answer, that's all.
turns.zh: 我能判断他们是从哪里学到这个定义的，仅此而已。他们不必给出我的答案，但千万别给出传统的特性团队的答案，这才是关键。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Do you have a favorite product that you recently discovered that you really love, whether it's software or something physical, something around the house?
turns.zh: 最近有没有特别喜欢的产品，无论是软件还是实体产品，比如家居用品？

turns.speaker: Marty Cagan
turns.en: I recently got a Rivian, which is amazing that they did an absolutely beautiful job. They're the Airbnb of car companies because the founder's a designer and imagine if a designer designed the next generation car. It's a phenomenally good job.
turns.zh: 我最近买了一辆Rivian，他们做得太棒了。他们是汽车公司的Airbnb，因为创始人是设计师。想象一下，如果让设计师来设计下一代汽车会怎样？这真是出色的工作。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Wow. I was imagining you could rent people's cars and that sounds pretty cool, but you mean it in a different way. Interestingly, both you and [inaudible 01:20:38] from Meta both had cars as your favorite recent product discovery. He had a Mercedes-Benz. And I made the joke that I hope to give away these products someday and the budget is blowing up with all these cars in the mix.
turns.zh: 哇。我之前还想象能租别人家的车用，听起来挺酷的，但你说的意思不一样。有趣的是，你和Meta的[音频缺失01:20:38]都把汽车列为最近最喜欢的产品发现。他买的是奔驰车。我开玩笑说希望未来能把这些产品送人，结果现在预算因为这么多车爆了。

turns.speaker: Marty Cagan
turns.en: Well, my favorite thing to do is ride motorcycles and there is a new generation of product that who knows, might save my life one day, but these are literally wireless airbag vests that you wear and it uses AI technology and sensors to decide if it should deploy. Luckily, mine has never had to go off, but I know for a lot of people it saved their lives. That's an example of technology where without the technology, it's a very vulnerable... Even with it, it's vulnerable.
turns.zh: 嗯，我最喜欢做的事就是骑摩托车。现在有一款新一代产品，说不定哪天能救我的命，但这是一款无线气囊背心，你戴着它，AI技术和传感器会判断是否需要展开。幸运的是，我的背心还没用过，但我知道对很多人来说，它确实救了命。这就是科技的例子，没有这项技术，人就很脆弱……即便有科技加持，也依然脆弱。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Wait, do you ride motorcycles?
turns.zh: 等等，你骑摩托车吗？

turns.speaker: Marty Cagan
turns.en: I do.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I had no idea. What bike do you ride?
turns.zh: 我完全不知道。你骑什么摩托车？

turns.speaker: Marty Cagan
turns.en: I have two and they're both BMWs.
turns.zh: 我有两辆，都是宝马的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Wow. We need to see a picture of this somewhere. That's amazing. I had no idea. Two final questions. Do you have a favorite life motto that you often come back to, share with friends or family and find useful either in work or in life?
turns.zh: 哇。我们得找个机会看看照片。这太棒了。我真没想到。最后两个问题：你有没有一句常挂在嘴边的人生格言，经常和朋友或家人分享，并且在工作或生活中觉得很有用？

turns.speaker: Marty Cagan
turns.en: I don't really have a life motto, but I do have one I share a lot with people because as you might imagine, I think writing really helps me think and I encourage other people to develop their thinking skills and there's a great quote from Leslie Lamport, the guy who... You're not old enough to know this, but he invented one of the first word processors called LaTeX, which I used to use back in the day. But if you're thinking without writing, you just think you're thinking.
turns.zh: 我倒没有什么人生格言，但我确实经常和别人分享这个观点，因为你可能能想象得到，我觉得写作真的能帮助我思考，我也鼓励其他人培养自己的思考能力。这里有一句莱斯利·兰波特（Leslie Lamport）说的话，他……你应该还不够大，可能不认识他，但他发明了最早的文字处理软件之一，叫LaTeX，我以前用过。不过如果你不写下来就只是自以为在思考。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: There's a version of this that I love and it's the same idea that I don't know what I think until I've written it down. I think Joan Didion said that.
turns.zh: 我特别喜欢这个观点，也是同样的道理——直到写下来我才知道自己在想什么。我觉得琼·迪迪翁（Joan Didion）也说过这句话。

turns.speaker: Marty Cagan
turns.en: Same idea.
turns.zh: 同样的道理。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And I so agree. That's why I started writing. I just want to figure this out that I have in my head. Crystallizing something that makes sense. Last question. You've been doing this work for many, many years now. How many years have you been at this?
turns.zh: 我完全赞同。这就是我开始写作的原因。我只是想理清自己脑子里的思路。把有意义的东西具象化。最后一个问题：你做这份工作很多年了，具体多少年？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: 43 years. What else would you have been doing right now if not having gone down this track?
turns.zh: 43年。要是当初没选择这条路，你现在会做什么？

turns.speaker: Marty Cagan
turns.en: Oh, well, honestly, I would've been really happy just staying in engineering. I've always loved design too. I think I would've been really happy as a designer. I think no matter what though, I would have been still building something, whether if it was houses or cars or whatever. I like building things.
turns.zh: 哦，说实话，我会很乐意继续待在工程领域。我一直也喜欢设计。我觉得自己做设计也会很开心。但无论如何，我都会继续创造些什么东西，无论是房子、汽车还是其他东西。我喜欢动手创造。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I love that. You're essentially a one man triad team in this dream. Marty, this was incredible. It was everything I was hoping it'd be. We covered so much stuff. I think we're going to help a lot of people transform. Two final questions, where can folks find your book? When is it available? Where can they reach out if they want to follow up on stuff? And how can listeners be useful to you?
turns.zh: 太棒了。你基本上就是这个梦想中的全能三人组。马蒂，这次访谈太棒了。完全超出了我的预期。我们聊了很多内容。我觉得我们能帮助很多人实现转变。最后两个问题：读者在哪里能找到你的书？什么时候上线？如果想跟进相关内容该怎么联系？听众如何能为你提供帮助？

turns.speaker: Marty Cagan
turns.en: The book should be available worldwide in electronic Kindle audio and hardback on March 12th. We'll see, but that's what the publishers promise. And you can find about all of the things I talk about and all our stuff is for free on the website, svpg.com, Silicon Valley Product Group. And if you don't know at least one of the partners, you should try to meet one. We all love meeting the community and I think you'll enjoy it. So hopefully that's useful.
turns.zh: 这本书应该在3月12日全球上线，有电子版、音频版和纸质版。我们拭目以待，但出版商是这么承诺的。你可以在svpg.com（硅谷产品集团）网站上免费获取我提到的所有内容。要是你们至少不认识一个合作伙伴，那应该去认识一下。我们都很乐意与社区交流，相信你们也会乐在其中。希望这些信息对你们有用。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: We've had two partners so far. We'll work our way through the rest over time. And I want to make sure you answer the last question, how can listeners be useful to you?
turns.zh: 到目前为止我们已经有两个合作伙伴了。我们会陆续介绍其他合作伙伴。最后再回答最后一个问题：听众如何能为你提供帮助？

turns.speaker: Marty Cagan
turns.en: To be honest, a lot of the inspiration for what we write comes from questions from people, and so we love it when people read something and if it works, great, and they tell us, we love that too. But if they have follow-up questions, one of the nice things about the online archive is we'll just go update the article to address the question. So we love that.
turns.zh: 老实说，我们写作的很多灵感都来自于读者的问题。所以当人们读完一篇文章后，如果觉得有用，那太棒了，他们能告诉我们，我们也特别开心。但如果他们还有后续问题，线上档案库的好处之一就是我们可以随时更新文章来解答这些问题。这点我们也很乐意。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: You do the same thing.
turns.zh: 你也可以这么做。

turns.speaker: Marty Cagan
turns.en: So feel free.
turns.zh: 所以别客气。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: All right. Amazing. Marty, thank you so much for making time to do this and for being here.
turns.zh: 好的，太棒了。马蒂，非常感谢你抽出时间参与节目，也感谢你的到来。

turns.speaker: Marty Cagan
turns.en: Thank you, Lenny.
turns.zh: 谢谢你，莱尼。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Bye everyone. Thank you so much for listening. turns.zh: 大家再见了。非常感谢聆听。如果你觉得这期节目有价值，可以在Apple Podcasts、Spotify或你喜欢的播客应用上订阅我们的节目。另外，请考虑给我们评分或留下评论，这真的能帮助其他听众找到我们的节目。你可以在lennyspodcast.com上查看往期节目或了解更多信息。下期节目再见。
